properties.areaDesc: Lower Koyukuk Valley; Middle Yukon Valley; Upper Koyukuk Valley; Dalton Highway Summits; White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River; Upper Chena River Valley; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills; Chatanika River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area; Nenana; Central Interior
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 3 at 11:18AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Central Interior-Nenana-Two Rivers-Middle Yukon Valley-Upper Koyukuk
Valley-Upper Chena River Valley-Fairbanks Metro Area-Goldstream
Valley and Nenana Hills-Lower Koyukuk Valley-Dalton Highway
Summits-Chatanika River Valley-White Mountains and High Terrain South
of the Yukon River-Eielson AFB and Salcha

Areas of 1 to 2.5 inches of rainfall are expected over the next 48
hours due to an atmospheric river. Average return intervals of 2 to 5
years is possible throughout much of the central and western interior
through the weekend. Isolated areas could potentially see heavy
rainfall more in line with 10 to even 25 year return intervals,
resulting in significant rises in the smaller headwater streams that
feed the Koyukuk and Middle Yukon Rivers. While there are no
immediate concerns for the main stem rivers in the area, they will
also see significant rises in water levels through the week as a
result of the expected heavy rainfall with sandbars potentially
becoming covered with water.

Across the Chena River basin, moderate to heavy rainfall of up to 1.5
inches is expected. This will also result in rises along the Chena
and Little Chena rivers. At this time flooding is not expected, but
should the focus for heaviest rainfall shift further east with time,
this could change.

Rainfall rates are expected to decrease by Sunday afternoon across
most of the area.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 3 at 12:11PM PDT until September 8 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 8 feet with dangerous rip currents, largest on south-facing
shores.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Saturday to 11 PM PDT Tuesday, peaking Monday
and Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Enhanced beach
erosion will occur. Flooding of sea water is likely, around the
time of high tide, over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such
as parking lots, beaches, and walkways. Significant damage to
roads or structures is NOT expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will occur around 5pm on
Saturday, 6pm on Sunday, 7pm on Monday, and 8pm on Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks. Follow advice from local
officials. Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.
